(Currently Amended) A method of impeding Leishmania transmission in humans by administering to a human subject a composition comprising a Fucose Mannose Ligand (FML) fraction derived from Leishmania donovani promastigotes or amastigotes and saponin, wherein the FML fraction comprises a glycoprotein complex containing 29% of neutral sugar, 44% of protein, 11% of phosphate and hexoamines traces composed by protein bands with molecular weight ranging from 9 to 95 kDa, some protein bands having carbohydrates at 36 and 54 to 68 kDa, the FML glycidic portion presenting 10% of fucose and 47% of mannose, 30% of glucose, 12% of galactose and xylose traces, amino acids containing 10 to 20% of glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid and glycine, 5 to 10% of serine, histidine, lysine, leucine, threonine, proline and valine, and 2 to 5% of arginine, methionine, isoleucine, tyrosine and phenylalanine, and wherein said composition is administered in a dose and formulation effective to induce blocking antibodies in humans that reduce transmission of Leishmania parasites by sandfly vectors.
